data.passageTitle: The Invention of the Television Part One
data.passage:
Televisions can be found in homes all across the world, but that was not always the case.

The first kind of television invented was primitive. One of these gadgets sent pictures through wires and the rotation of a metal disk. The inventors themselves called it an electric telescope, and it was nothing like the televisions we have today. However, these early TVs led the way for the next wave of inventors whose contraptions would be called electronic televisions.

To whom do we credit the invention of the first electronic television? The answer to that question can be difficult to fathom.

The person who accomplished this great advancement in 1927 was only 21 years old! His last name was Farnsworth. He lived in a house that did not even have electricity until he was 14 years old.
